The *Upasamātherīgāthā* (Thig 1.10) is a single-verse poem located in the opening chapter (*Ekakanipāta*) of the *Therīgāthā*, the canonical collection of verses attributed to early Buddhist elder nuns (*therī*s) in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Attributed to the nun Upasamā, the verse forms part of the traditional core of early Buddhist women's poetry.
Neither SuttaCentral's curated comparative data nor automated text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus record any external or internal parallels, identifying no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. All passages retrieved from the secondary literature dossier merely match occurrences of the homonymous doctrinal noun *upasama* ("calm" or "tranquillity", as in *upasamānussati* or *prapañcopaśama*) and do not discuss the text itself.
